outline.description: This chapter introduces the necessity of adapting large foundation models to downstream tasks and provides an overview of existing parameter-efficient finetuning strategies.
subtopics: The challenge of training foundation models from scratch
Overview of PEFT categories: Model Finetuning, Adapter Tuning, and Prompt Tuning
The trade-off between parameter efficiency and model performance
Introduction to the goal of preserving pretraining knowledge during adaptation

outline.description: An exploration of the core principles behind Orthogonal Finetuning, explaining why orthogonality is used to preserve semantic knowledge.
subtopics: The concept of preserving pairwise angles between neurons
Mathematical formulation of OFT: The multiplicative orthogonal update
The role of the identity matrix in zero initialization
Limitations of block-diagonal structures in OFT: Parameter efficiency vs. expressivity

outline.description: This chapter explains the theoretical framework used to rethink matrix factorization as a graph-based information flow problem.
subtopics: Mapping matrix multiplication to grid-structured graphs
Interpreting dense matrices as full connectivity between source and receiver nodes
Desiderata for efficient factorization: Dense connectivity and minimum free edges
The impact of orthogonality constraints on graph edges

outline.description: A deep dive into the technical implementation of BOFT, focusing on butterfly structures and how they enable dense orthogonal matrices with few parameters.
subtopics: Inspiration from the Cooley-Tukey Fast Fourier Transform (FFT)
Defining the Butterfly Factor and the recursive Butterfly Matrix
Block Butterfly Components and their construction
Complexity analysis: $O(d^2)$ vs. $O(d)$ vs. $O(d log d)$ parameters
Generalizing BOFT: From block-diagonal OFT to full orthogonal matrices

outline.description: This chapter covers the mathematical tools and training techniques required to make BOFT stable and effective in practice.
subtopics: Maintaining orthogonality via the Cayley Transform
Identity initialization strategies for weight preservation
Multiplicative Dropout: Adapting dropout for multiplicative weight updates
The training pipeline: From frozen pretrained weights to learned butterfly components

outline.chapter_title: Theoretical Insights: Expressivity and Spectral Properties
outline.description: An analysis of the mathematical advantages of BOFT, including its approximation capabilities and its effect on training stability.
subtopics: Expressivity: Comparing BOFT and block-diagonal OFT
The Kaleidoscope Hierarchy: Approximating the full orthogonal group
Spectral Norm Preservation: Why orthogonal updates improve training stability
Inductive Bias: The relationship between butterfly structures and classic linear transforms (Fourier, Hadamard)

outline.description: An examination of BOFT's performance across various AI domains, demonstrating its versatility as a generic finetuning method.
subtopics: Adapting Large Language Models (LLMs)
Finetuning Large Vision Transformers (ViTs)
Controllable Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
Comparative analysis: BOFT vs. LoRA and standard OFT
